ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is a positive point charge labeled 1 nC, and two rays are drawn from the position of this charge; the shorter ray points to point Q and is labeled with a distance of 20 mm; the longer ray points to point P and is labeled with a distance of 40 mm. Reasoning: Convert the distances to meters, r_P = 40 mm = 0.04 m, r_Q = 20 mm = 0.02 m. The point charge potential formula is V = q/(4πϵr), where q = +1×10^-9 C, ϵ = 8.85×10^-12 F/m. First calculate the constant term q/(4πϵ) ≈ 8.99. Thus V_P ≈ 8.99/0.04 = 224.8 V, V_Q ≈ 8.99/0.02 = 449.6 V. According to V_PQ = V_P - V_Q, obtain V_PQ ≈ 224.8 - 449.6 = -224.8 V, approximately -225 V. Since Q is closer to the positive charge, the potential is higher, so V_P - V_Q is negative.
